steps.sceneEditorDesc: This is your scene editor. Build your story by adding dialogue, choices, and effects to each scene.
steps.livePreviewDesc: See your visual novel in real-time as you build it. Changes appear instantly!
steps.assetsDesc: Manage your characters, backgrounds, music, and images in the asset panels.
steps.commandPaletteDesc: Add dialogue, choices, branching paths, sound effects, and 30+ other commands to your scenes.
steps.gameSettingsDesc: Configure your game's resolution, title, author info, and starting scene.

helpPanel.title: Help & Reference
helpPanel.noResultsHint: Try searching for a command name, category, or keyword.

gs.step1Desc: From the Project Hub, click "New Project" to start fresh or open an existing .zip project file.
gs.step2Desc: Use the Scenes tab to create scenes. Each scene contains a sequence of commands that make up your story.
gs.step3Desc: Inside a scene, add commands like Dialogue, ShowCharacter, and SetBackground to build your visual novel.
gs.step4Desc: Use the Characters tab to create characters with expressions, and the Assets tab to import backgrounds, images, and audio.
gs.step5Desc: Click "Play" to preview your game live. When ready, use "Export" to save as .zip or "Build" to create a standalone game.

tips.organizeTip: Break your story into logical scenes. Each scene should represent a distinct location, conversation, or event. This makes it easier to navigate and edit your project.
tips.variablesTip: Track player choices with variables (e.g., "friendshipLevel", "route"). Use conditions to create branching paths based on these values for a more dynamic story.
tips.previewTip: Use the Play button frequently to test your scenes. This helps catch dialogue errors, missing transitions, and pacing issues early.
tips.audioTip: Combine background music with sound effects for immersive scenes. Use fade-in/out durations for smooth audio transitions between scenes.
tips.labelsTip: Instead of duplicating content, use Label and JumpToLabel commands to create loops within a scene — great for retry mechanics or repeated dialogue.
tips.stackingTip: Use the async modifier on commands to run them in parallel. This lets you show a character, change background, and play music all at once for cinematic moments.
tips.branchesTip: Use BranchStart/BranchEnd to visually group related commands in the editor. Color-code branches to quickly identify different story routes.
tips.effectsTip: Combine ShakeScreen, FlashScreen, and TintScreen effects with sound effects for impactful dramatic moments like explosions or revelations.

Dialogue.desc: Display character dialogue with optional speaker name and portrait.
Dialogue.example: Show Sakura saying "Hello!" on the left side of the screen.

Choice.desc: Present the player with multiple options that affect the story path.
Choice.example: Ask the player "Where do you go?" with options "Park", "Library", "Home".

BranchStart.desc: Begin a named branch section for organizing story paths visually.
BranchStart.example: Start a branch called "Sakura Route" colored pink to group related commands.

BranchEnd.desc: End a previously opened branch section.

ShowCharacter.desc: Display a character sprite on screen with position and expression.
ShowCharacter.example: Show Kai at center position with happy expression, fading in over 0.5 seconds.

HideCharacter.desc: Remove a character from the screen with a transition.
HideCharacter.example: Hide Sakura with a fade-out transition over 1 second.

SetBackground.desc: Change the background image of the scene.
SetBackground.example: Set background to "school_hallway" with crossfade over 1 second.

ShowText.desc: Display text overlay on screen at a specific position with styling.
ShowText.example: Show "Chapter 1" centered on screen in large white text, fading in.

HideText.desc: Remove a previously shown text overlay from the screen.
HideText.example: Hide the chapter title text with a fade-out.

ShowImage.desc: Display an image overlay on screen with position, size, and rotation.
ShowImage.example: Show a letter image centered on screen at 50% size, fading in.

HideImage.desc: Remove a previously shown image overlay from the screen.
HideImage.example: Hide the letter image with a fade-out transition.

ShowButton.desc: Display an interactive button on screen with styling and click actions.
ShowButton.example: Show a "Continue" button at the bottom center that jumps to the next scene when clicked.

HideButton.desc: Remove a previously shown button from the screen.
HideButton.example: Hide the "Continue" button with a fade-out.

ShowImageMap.desc: Display an image with clickable hot-spot regions that trigger actions (jump, set variable).
ShowImageMap.example: Show a world map image with clickable city regions that jump to different scenes when clicked.

HideImageMap.desc: Remove a previously shown image map from the screen.
HideImageMap.example: Hide the world map with a fade-out transition.

PlayMusic.desc: Start playing background music. Loops by default.

StopMusic.desc: Stop the currently playing background music.
StopMusic.example: Stop music with a 1 second fade-out.

PlaySoundEffect.example: Play door_knock sound at full volume.

StopSoundEffect.desc: Stop all currently playing sound effects.

PlayMovie.desc: Play a video file. In fullscreen mode, shows over a black background (cutscenes). In overlay mode, plays transparently on top of the scene (effects like falling petals, rain).
PlayMovie.example: Play falling petals as a looping transparent overlay while dialogue continues underneath.

StopMovie.desc: Stop all currently playing movie overlays.
StopMovie.example: Stop the falling petals overlay when the scene changes.

SetVariable.desc: Set a game variable to a value. Used for tracking choices and stats.

TextInput.desc: Ask the player to type text input and store it in a variable.
TextInput.example: Ask "What is your name?" and store the answer in "playerName".

Label.desc: Define a named label point within a scene that can be jumped to.
Label.example: Create a label called "loop_start" to mark a return point.

JumpToLabel.desc: Jump to a named label within the current scene.
JumpToLabel.example: Jump back to the "loop_start" label to repeat a section.

Wait.desc: Pause for a specified duration before continuing.
Wait.example: Wait 2 seconds before showing next dialogue, or wait for player click.

ShowScreen.desc: Display a custom UI screen (menus, inventories, etc.).

ShakeScreen.desc: Apply a screen shake effect for dramatic impact.
ShakeScreen.example: Shake the screen for 0.5 seconds at medium intensity during an explosion.

TintScreen.desc: Apply a color tint overlay to the entire screen.
TintScreen.example: Tint the screen red over 1 second to indicate danger.

FlashScreen.desc: Flash the screen with a bright color for a brief moment.
FlashScreen.example: Flash the screen white for 0.3 seconds for a lightning effect.

PanZoomScreen.desc: Pan and zoom the camera to focus on a specific area.
PanZoomScreen.example: Zoom in 2x on the left side of the screen over 1 second.

ResetScreenEffects.desc: Reset all active screen effects (tint, zoom, etc.) back to normal.
ResetScreenEffects.example: Reset all screen effects smoothly over 0.5 seconds.

SetScreenOverlayEffect.desc: Apply a persistent overlay effect like rain, snow, or particles.
SetScreenOverlayEffect.example: Add a gentle snowfall effect at 50% intensity.

Group.desc: Group multiple events together for visual organization in the editor.
Group.example: Group the "enter classroom" events (background, characters, music) together.
